answer: The protocol's dynamic opportunity-cost bond, anchored in basalt derived hash-time commitments, forces each identity to lock staking collateral proportional to its zero-knowledge verifiable delay proof. An adversary attempting to forge additional Sybil nodes faces a subgame-perfect slashing matrix that scales penalties exponentially with the delay exponent, rendering expected attack utility strictly negative. Consequently, the grove of rational validators converges to a strict Nash equilibrium where any unilateral deviation reduces payoff.
